selected_evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (configuration)
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline showed no /etc/cron.allow; opsadmin created and /etc/cron.allow written with root and opsadmin, cron.deny removed, crond restarted active.

selected_evidence.requirement: Functional proof: root and opsadmin can schedule; other users cannot
selected_evidence.summary: root and opsadmin successfully installed/listed crontabs; a test unprivileged user was denied with 'not allowed to use this program (crontab)', then removed.
Captured boot_id 83a0a80f-773c-4f3e-9137-1e7aa887b07a, crond active, cron.allow contents (root, opsadmin), cron.deny absent.
systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded nohup; command acknowledged and connection subsequently dropped (stream closed), confirming reboot proceeded.

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
selected_evidence.summary: Node unreachable during reboot (timeout, connection reset), then reachable again with new boot_id df4b7e15-ff02-42de-a66b-18b9a459b1d9 and fresh uptime, differing from the pre-restart boot_id.

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron service, config, and access control
selected_evidence.summary: crond active post-restart, /etc/cron.allow persisted with root/opsadmin, cron.deny still absent, root and opsadmin successfully scheduled/removed crontabs, and a newly created unlisted test user was denied crontab access, matching pre-restart behavior.

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "== OS =="; cat /etc/os-release | head -3
echo "== cron service =="; (systemctl list-units --type=service | grep -i cron) || true
echo "== cron.allow/deny =="; ls -l /etc/cron.allow /etc/cron.deny 2>&1 || true
echo "== users =="; getent passwd root opsadmin 2>&1 || true
echo "== crontab bin =="; which crontab || true

commands.command:
set -Eeuo pipefail
echo "STEP: baseline crond status"
sudo -n systemctl is-active crond

echo "STEP: create opsadmin user if missing"
if ! getent passwd opsadmin >/dev/null; then
  sudo -n useradd -m -s /bin/bash opsadmin
  echo "opsadmin created"
else
  echo "opsadmin already exists"
fi

echo "STEP: create test-denied user for verification"
if ! getent passwd cronreject_test >/dev/null; then
  sudo -n useradd -m -s /bin/bash cronreject_test
fi

echo "STEP: write /etc/cron.allow"
printf 'root\nopsadmin\n' | sudo -n tee /etc/cron.allow >/dev/null
sudo -n chown root:root /etc/cron.allow
sudo -n chmod 644 /etc/cron.allow

echo "STEP: remove /etc/cron.deny (cron.allow takes precedence; remove for clarity)"
sudo -n rm -f /etc/cron.deny

echo "STEP: restart crond"
sudo -n systemctl restart crond
sudo -n systemctl is-active crond

echo "STEP: verify cron.allow contents"
cat /etc/cron.allow
ls -l /etc/cron.allow

echo "STEP: verify root can use cron"
sudo -n crontab -l -u root 2>&1 || echo "root has no crontab yet (ok)"
echo "test job" | sudo -n crontab -u root - 
sudo -n crontab -l -u root

echo "STEP: verify opsadmin can use cron"
echo "* * * * * echo hi" | sudo -n crontab -u opsadmin -
sudo -n crontab -l -u opsadmin

echo "STEP: verify non-listed user is denied"
set +e
sudo -n -u cronreject_test crontab -l 2>&1
RC1=$?
echo "test-user list rc=$RC1"
echo "* * * * * echo hi" | sudo -n -u cronreject_test crontab - 2>&1
RC2=$?
echo "test-user install rc=$RC2"
set -e
if [ "$RC2" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "FAIL: non-listed user was able to install a cron job"
  exit 1
fi
echo "PASS: non-listed user denied cron access"

echo "STEP: cleanup test user"
sudo -n userdel -r cronreject_test 2>&1 || true
